instalacoesEReformas.title: Instalações e Reformas
instalacoesEReformas.description: Case study of a service platform ecosystem at Leroy Merlin, covering partner onboarding, customer journeys, orchestration, observability, and technical leadership.

hero.subtitle: A service ecosystem for selling, scheduling, and operating installations and home reforms with reliability across customer, partner, and internal journeys.
hero.summary: This case study reflects the point in my career where I moved from frontend ownership into broader technical leadership, working across backend, infrastructure, observability, release discipline, and product delivery for a business-critical ecosystem.

overview.title: Project overview
overview.intro: An ecosystem built to connect customers, partner professionals, and Leroy Merlin operations around service delivery.
paragraphs: Instalacoes e Reformas was not just a single frontend application. It was a broader service ecosystem involving public pages, operational flows, partner onboarding, and internal tools that supported how installations and reforms were offered and executed.

The project required product thinking, technical consistency, and operational reliability because the experience touched different types of users and depended on stable communication between multiple services and teams.

businessProblem.title: Business problem
businessProblem.intro: The challenge was to make service operations understandable, scalable, and trustworthy for everyone involved.
paragraphs: Selling a service is more complex than selling a physical product. The platform needed to communicate trust, explain the service clearly, support operational rules, and create flows that worked for customers, business stakeholders, and partner professionals.
That meant reducing friction in acquisition and onboarding journeys while also giving the internal ecosystem enough structure to evolve without creating operational chaos.

scopeAndComplexity.title: Scope and complexity
scopeAndComplexity.intro: The complexity came from scale, integration, and the fact that the ecosystem blended product, operations, and architecture concerns.
paragraphs: My work eventually touched more than 40 microservices and multiple frontend experiences. It was a context where changes in one part of the ecosystem could affect partner flows, customer communication, or internal operations.
The platform also had to support different environments, release flows, and technical decisions across a growing architecture, which made engineering discipline as important as feature delivery.
items: Customer-facing flows and public pages connected to service acquisition
Partner and onboarding experiences with operational dependencies
Distributed architecture with frontend and backend services evolving in parallel
Cross-team coordination involving product, engineering, and business stakeholders

myRole.title: My role in the project
myRole.intro: I started in the frontend and grew into a tech lead role with broader responsibility for delivery quality and technical direction.
paragraphs: Over time, I stopped being focused only on UI implementation and started supporting the ecosystem from a wider engineering perspective. I worked on frontend architecture, backend participation with Java and Spring Boot, infrastructure support on Google Cloud Platform, and observability initiatives.

I also supported technical decisions, helped organize codebases and folder structures, contributed to cleaner engineering standards, and worked closely with the team to keep the ecosystem maintainable while delivery kept moving.
items: Technical leadership for service evolution and cross-team delivery
Hands-on contribution in React/Next.js frontend applications
Backend support in Java and Spring Boot microservices
Guidance on architecture, clean code, and implementation standards

architecture.title: Architecture and technologies
architecture.intro: The ecosystem combined modern frontend delivery with backend services, observability, and release automation.
paragraphs: On the frontend, I worked with React-based applications, public pages, and operational experiences that needed clarity, performance, and maintainability. On the backend side, I participated in Java and Spring Boot services, helping with structure, clean code, and technical direction.

The operational side of the project also involved environment organization, semantic versioning, GitHub Actions workflows, Datadog monitoring, and support for event-driven evolution where service communication and long-term scalability mattered.
items: Support for Google Cloud Platform environments and application lifecycle organization
Datadog monitors for backend and frontend incidents and error visibility
GitHub Actions workflows for unit tests, pull request feedback, deploy flows, and release discipline
Technical support for diagrams, architecture discussions, and service communication improvements

contributions.title: Main contributions
contributions.intro: My contribution was not limited to one layer of the stack. It was about making the ecosystem easier to evolve and safer to operate.
paragraphs: A large part of my work was improving engineering consistency, helping the team move faster with more confidence, and reducing ambiguity around how applications should be structured, delivered, and monitored.
items: Supported architecture decisions across a distributed ecosystem with multiple services
Helped define clean frontend and backend structures for scalability and maintainability
Created GitHub Actions workflows for unit tests, pull request feedback, and deployment support
Organized environments and release practices with semantic versioning and clearer delivery governance
Created Datadog monitors to increase visibility into backend and frontend failures

challenges.title: Challenges
challenges.intro: The project demanded technical depth and operational awareness at the same time.
paragraphs: One of the main challenges was balancing short-term business needs with long-term technical quality in an ecosystem with many dependencies. Another was making sure frontend, backend, and operational concerns were aligned enough that releases stayed reliable.
items: Keeping consistency across many services, teams, and delivery cadences
Improving observability and incident awareness in a distributed environment
Supporting architecture evolution without blocking product demands
Translating technical constraints into decisions that made sense for business and operations

results.title: Results and impact
results.intro: The impact showed up in delivery maturity, technical reliability, and a more structured ecosystem.
paragraphs: The work helped strengthen the quality of releases, increase visibility into failures, and improve the engineering foundation behind the service experience. That created better conditions for scaling the ecosystem and supporting ongoing product evolution.
Just as important, the project gave me a stronger ability to connect code quality, platform decisions, and operational reality in a business-facing environment.
items: Better release discipline with clearer workflows and versioning
Improved monitoring and faster visibility into backend and frontend issues
Stronger technical standards for frontend and backend implementation
More confidence in delivery across a business-critical service ecosystem

learnings.title: Learnings
learnings.intro: This was one of the experiences that most expanded my understanding of technical leadership.
paragraphs: I learned how much value comes from connecting architecture, observability, release discipline, and communication instead of treating them as separate concerns. I also strengthened my ability to support decisions beyond the frontend while staying practical and delivery-oriented.
items: Leadership grows when you can connect product, engineering, and operations
Scalability depends on standards, visibility, and decision clarity as much as on code
Good technical direction reduces friction for both teams and business stakeholders
Reliable delivery is built through systems, not isolated heroics

me.title: About Me
me.description: Learn more about my background, skills, and experience.
content: I am a software engineer and tech lead with more than five years of experience building digital products, internal platforms, and scalable service ecosystems. My work has grown from frontend development into a broader technical scope that includes backend, infrastructure, observability, architecture support, and delivery leadership.

In recent years, I have worked in contexts where customer journeys, partner operations, and internal systems needed to evolve together. That pushed me to act across frontend architecture, Java and Spring Boot backend services, and technical decisions that balanced business needs with maintainability.

I also worked with Google Cloud Platform, observability in Datadog, monitor creation for backend and frontend error tracking, GitHub Actions workflows for unit tests, pull request feedback, deployment pipelines, semantic versioning, and environment organization across development and production.

My main strengths include web application development, technical decision support, delivery planning, communication between technical and non-technical stakeholders, debugging, quality practices, and building solutions that connect engineering discipline with business reality.

I have a degree in Systems Analysis and Development from FATEC and an IT technician from ETEC. I am passionate about web application development and automation, and I am always looking to learn new technologies and methodologies.

I am a committed, creative, and collaborative professional, who likes to work as a team and solve problems. I am proud to have been awarded at two innovation events, Ideathon and Inovathon São Paulo, where I presented solutions to the challenges of the digital environment and culture and tourism. My goal is to continue developing solutions that generate value for customers and society.

personalManifesto.title: Personal Manifesto
personalManifesto.description: My core values and principles that guide my work and life.
content: **I don't seek to be perfect. I seek to be whole.**
I want to understand before judging, build before criticizing, and feel before deciding.
My mind works like a system: I like to see the logic, the flows, the patterns. But my heart doesn't accept automatisms. It pulls me back to meaning — to what is just, human, true.
I push myself because I care. I pay attention to details because I know the weight of consequences. Sometimes this overwhelms me. But I don't regret trying to do things right.

I observe the world with attention. I like well-placed silences, honest conversations, and ideas that have foundation. I like to create things that speak for me, that express what doesn't fit in words.
**I don't want to control everything — I want to understand better.**
**I don't want to convince everyone — I want to be understood.**
*And if something I do touches someone, then it was worth it.*
